title: Research
text: My work connects sociology, cognitive science and computational approaches to investigate how knowledge is produced, evaluated, communicated and used in technologically mediated environments.

title: Research
text:
Social sciences and cognitive sciences
I develop research at the interface of social and cognitive sciences, with a particular interest in the micro-foundations of social and organizational processes. This includes reasoning, information search, learning, metacognition and epistemic evaluation.

title: Research
section: Digital technologies, artificial intelligence and big data
text:
Digital technologies, artificial intelligence and big data
My research examines artificial intelligence, algorithms, recommendation systems, big data and digital technologies as scientific, technical, organizational and social phenomena. Earlier work focused especially on digital markets, recommendation technologies, organizational digitalization and AI in professional settings.

title: Research
section: Information search, learning and epistemic vigilance
text:
Information search, learning and epistemic vigilance
A central current question is how people decide what deserves attention, trust, verification and integration into knowledge. I study how prior knowledge, information-search behaviour, social context and metacognitive judgments shape learning from documents and from other people.

title: Research
section: Computational modelling, multi-agent systems and epistemic injustice
text:
Computational modelling, multi-agent systems and epistemic injustice
I use agent-based modelling to examine how local cognitive and interactional mechanisms generate longer-term social and epistemic patterns. Current models investigate socially embedded learning, epistemic-credit allocation and cumulative inequalities.

title: Research
text:
MOVICI and CAVL
MOVICI — Modelling Epistemic Vigilance and its Institutions is the main current research programme. It combines empirical experiments, theoretical integration and computational modelling.
Open MOVICI ↗ UCA / DS4H project page ↗ MSHS / COCOLAB project page ↗
The programme currently includes five connected papers:

CAVL: A Cognitive Architecture for Vigilant Learning
Prior Knowledge and Learning from Open Web Search
Epistemic Credit in Cooperative and Competitive Debate
Learning from Documents and from Others: Knowledge Change and Epistemic Coordination
Epistemic Credit Misallocation in Socially Embedded Learning

title: Jean-Sébastien Vayre — Sociologist of AI, Digital Technologies & Cognition
text:
Associate Professor of Sociology · Université Côte d’Azur · GREDEG (UMR 7321 CNRS) · INNOS · Nice, France
I am a sociologist of digital technologies and artificial intelligence working at the intersection of social sciences and cognitive sciences. My research focuses on information search, learning, metacognition, epistemic vigilance, computational modelling and multi-agent systems, as well as organizational transformations associated with digital technologies.

title: Jean-Sébastien Vayre — Sociologist of AI, Digital Technologies & Cognition
text:
Current research
The main current programme is MOVICI, which combines a theoretical architecture (CAVL — Cognitive Architecture for Vigilant Learning), empirical studies of open-Web information search and cooperative/competitive debate, and agent-based modelling.
